NOVELTY STATEMENT — Standard practice tracks voltage efficiency and capacity fade directly. My observable is the vanadium crossover rate inferred from the differential pressure between half-cells, which directly measures the driving force for vanadium crossover before it manifests as capacity fade. This connects to failure physics via the pressure-driven transport of vanadium ions across the membrane, which precedes electrolyte imbalance.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is Fick's law of diffusion with pressure contribution: J = -D(ΔC/Δx) + (C·K·ΔP)/(η·Δx), where J is crossover flux, D is diffusion coefficient, C is concentration, K is membrane permeability, η is viscosity, and ΔP is pressure differential. For a Nafion 212 membrane at 1.5M vanadium concentration, a pressure differential of 5 kPa would cause a crossover rate of approximately 0.02 mA/cm², which would lead to the observed 15% capacity fade over 2000 cycles.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Components: Existing pressure sensors (±0.1 kPa accuracy) in half-cell headers, existing data acquisition system, existing electrolyte flow rate meters. Procedure: Calculate average pressure differential (ΔP) between half-cells during charge/discharge cycles. Compute vanadium crossover rate using membrane permeability constant for Nafion 212 (K = 1.2×10⁻¹² m²/Pa·s). No new hardware required; only software modification to existing monitoring system.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Installability: Same (uses existing sensors). Operability: Same (no additional operator actions required). Maintenance: Same (pressure sensors already maintained). Cost class: Same (no additional hardware). Expected conclusion: Same deployment burden, different observable that provides earlier warning of capacity fade.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Monitor pressure differential between half-cells during cycling. Instruments: Existing pressure sensors and data acquisition system. Pass threshold: ΔP < 3 kPa average over 100 cycles. Fail threshold: ΔP > 5 kPa sustained for 50 consecutive cycles. Duration: 500 cycles. Kill criterion: If ΔP exceeds 5 kPa for 50 consecutive cycles, the test fails and the approach is falsified.
